Given that the points $A$ and $B$ with coordinates $(3,5)$ and $(-3,-5),$ respectively, are the endpoints of a diameter of a circle centered at the origin, what is the equation of the circle?
worked_solution:
The equation of a circle with radius $r,$ centered at the origin, is 

$$
{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}={r}^{2}.
$$

First, we calculate the length of the diameter $\overset{―}{AB}:$

 

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =\sqrt{{(5-(-5))}^{2}+{(3-(-3))}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{10}^{2}+{6}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{136} \\  & =\sqrt{4\cdot 34} \\  & =2\sqrt{34}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $\overset{―}{AB}$ is a diameter, the radius is

$$
r=\frac{AB}{2}=\frac{2\sqrt{34}}{2}=\sqrt{34}.
$$

So, the equation of the circle is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2} & ={r}^{2} \\ {x}^{2}+{y}^{2} & =(\sqrt{34})^{2} \\ {x}^{2}+{y}^{2} & =34.\end{aligned}
$$
